Practice: Security only at the final release checkpoint
Why it is limited: Important weaknesses may be discovered after dependent work accumulates
Existing defensive alternative: Earlier feedback alongside release and operational safeguards

Why it is limited: A single compromise can cross project and environment boundaries
Existing defensive alternative: Narrow workload identities and context-specific permissions

Practice: Mutable external scripts in privileged jobs
Why it is limited: Retrieved code can change without a reviewed repository change
Existing defensive alternative: Controlled inputs, trusted integrity expectations, and isolated execution

Practice: Treat every warning as equally important
Why it is limited: Noise and missing context can undermine triage
Existing defensive alternative: Contextual prioritization, ownership, and documented exceptions

Practice: Treat a signature as proof of safe behavior
Why it is limited: Authenticated origin does not establish benign content
Existing defensive alternative: Verification of identity and production expectations alongside application assessment

Practice: Produce an SBOM only for an audit
Why it is limited: An unused or stale inventory does not support timely response
Existing defensive alternative: Connect component information to deployed artifacts and advisory handling

Why it is limited: Automation can repeatedly restore an unsafe intended state
Existing defensive alternative: Review desired configuration and observe actual infrastructure behavior

Practice: Treat alert generation as incident response
Why it is limited: A warning may have no owner or effective containment path
Existing defensive alternative: Actionable monitoring, assigned responsibility, and maintained response processes
